podcast.body: A very rare and distinctive limited edition cassette version of the *Blurryface* album, notable for its bright red color. "When the album was released, it came out in the usual ways, but there was also a limited edition cassette that was very, very red."

podcast.body: An instrumental version of the *Blurryface* album that mysteriously appeared in the UK. It is described as very hard to find and its official status (whether bootleg or legitimate) is uncertain. "There's also a blurry face instrumental album that popped up in the UK for some reason. It's very hard to find."

podcast.body: Highly collectible special vinyl editions of the *Blurryface* album, each uniquely produced with an inkblot design so that "no two are the same." These editions are highly sought after by fans and can trade for hundreds of dollars. "But fans really treasure the inkblot special vinyl editions."

podcast.body: This album contributed significantly to Twenty One Pilots becoming one of the top streaming artists in 2016, the year streaming generated more revenue for the American recorded music business than all other forms of music distribution combined. "If we go back to that year, we'll see that one of the top streaming artists of 2016 was these guys, thanks to their blurry face album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was identified as the biggest rock album of the 2010s, based on various metrics including sales and streams. It spent 234 weeks on the charts, held the number one position for nine weeks, and all its songs combined have been streamed 3.5 billion times. "The biggest rock album of the 2010s was Bluriface from 21 Pilots."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This fourth record, released in 2015, marked the band's major breakthrough and began a more mystical and complicated phase for the group. It explored themes of doubt, insecurity, anxiety, and religion through the character Blurryface. The album sold close to 2 million copies and produced six singles. "They blew up with the blurry face album in 2015."
